Using this historical power consumption data, Machine Learning models will then be trained to predict in real-time the power consumption footprint of each type of application, whether they be capacity (single-node jobs) or capability (large-scale, multi-node jobs) applications, or somewhere in between. Based on this prediction of the required power/energy footprints from the batch of scheduled jobs, an accurate estimate of the maximum amount of cooling resources needed can then be calculated. The cooling system can be ramped up ahead of time in anticipation of a large job coming online. Similarly, if the power consumption for the collection of jobs is expected to drop, then the cooling system will be ramped down at a prescribed rate in anticipation of the IT system ramping down. This ramping up/down of the cooling system can be done each day at the appropriate time, given the anticipated cooling needs of the job collection that’s expected to run or come online as scheduled. This approach, in addition, will in all likelihood also allow for a more accurate prediction of the daily/weekly PUE prediction, setting the stage for better resource utilizations at NREL. This will also allow us to concurrently optimize power utilization from the local utility. 9 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. NREL deliverables: • Use the SLURM scheduler to collect power consumption profiles for application jobs that are running on Eagle. • Determine the relationship between specific node types (e.g., GPU-based versus CPU- based nodes) and power usage based on different applications. • Determine the relationship between application power usage and cooling system ramp time, including amount and type of cooling resources. • Identify an AI model strategy to predict the cooling system ramp time in advance of some significant power usage by a job. • Identify an initial test case for predictive ramp up/down of the cooling system. HPE deliverables: HPE to work with NREL to develop AI-based models using historical application-level power consumption profiles to predict power usage profile for given jobs. NREL to provide all relevant data. Task 3.2.9: Instrumentation Resiliency, Integrity, and Anomaly Detection NREL’s data center is highly instrumented. The instrumentation can sometimes drift, or malfunction, in ways that are difficult to detect. This task will focus on characterizing and tracking instrumentation behavior over time. Anomalous behavior will be flagged after which servicing and maintenance can occur. NREL deliverables: • NREL to identify a select number of sensors to track. • For each sensor to be tracked, NREL should identify at least two correlated sensors.
